quantization: serialized scores are quantized to 12 decimal places with ROUND_HALF_EVEN; all calculations use Python Decimal with precision 34

cases.description: Single independent item, age 0, empty query context. q=0.9; P=0.89; E=2/3; M=0 (fewer than 3 independence groups in the bin); level capped at 2.
Two independent items with reliability 0.6 (perfect) and 0.3 (worst); P = (0.6*1 + 0.3*0)/0.9 = 2/3.
cases.derivation: p_A = 0.30+0.25+0.20+0.15+0.10 = 1; p_B = 0. Weights 0.6/0.9 and 0.3/0.9 give P = 2/3. E: e_A = 1/1.07 (cost 0.07), e_B = 0 (zero benefit), so E = (2/3)*(100/107) = 200/321. M has only 2 independence groups -> null bin.

cases.description: No evidence at all: P=M=E=0, U=1 everywhere, level 1, no promotion.
Every item lacks provenance: unscorable and reported separately.
Three items with reliability 0: zero total weight with reason ZERO_TOTAL_WEIGHT.
Non-empty query context fully disjoint from every item's tags: Jaccard 0.
Empty query context gives context_relevance=1 regardless of evidence tags.
Query {a,b}: Jaccard 1/2, 1, and 2/3 for the three items.
An exact duplicate (larger evidence_id) is represented once; scores equal score-001 exactly.
cases.derivation: e0002 is byte-identical to e0001 except evidence_id, so exact-duplicate dedup retains e0001 only; the result equals score-001: P=0.89, E=2/3.

cases.description: Four items sharing one independence_key get independence 1/sqrt(4)=0.5 each; one independent item added. All p_j=1 so P=1 regardless of weights.
cases.derivation: independence = 1/sqrt(4) = 0.5 exactly; sum(q_P) = 4*0.5 + 1 = 3, so U_P = 1/sqrt(4) = 0.5 exactly. P = 1 (weighted mean of identical p_j=1). Two distinct groups cap level at 2.

cases.description: Descendant evidence at depth 2 is divided by (1+2)=3: weights 0.9 and 0.3 give P = 0.75.
The p_j=0 item is exactly h_P=90 days old, so its P weight decays by 1/2: P = (1*1 + 0.5*0)/1.5 = 2/3.
cases.derivation: decay = exp(-ln(2)*90/90) = 0.5; weights 1 and 0.5 give P = 2/3. For M (h=30) the stale item decays to exp(-3*ln2)=0.125; for E (h=7) to exp(-ln2*90/7).

cases.description: Evidence from the future is invalid and counted under other exclusions.
Contradiction only enters through the 0.10*(1-contradiction) term: equal weights, p in {1.0, 0.9}, so P = 0.95.
cases.derivation: p_A = 1, p_B = 1 - 0.10 = 0.9; equal weights give P = 0.95 exactly.

cases.description: Four independent items in bin u=0.8, quality 0.9 >= 0.70, S=0.5: M = 0.8*0.5 = 0.4.
cases.derivation: w=1/4 each; Q=0.9 (eligible); S = sum(w*1*0.5) = 0.5; M = 0.8*0.5 = 0.4 exactly; selected_m_bin=0.8 with 4 items. P=1 (all p_j=1); E: benefit=0.5, cost=0.07, e = 0.5/0.57 = 50/57.

cases.description: Only 2 distinct independence groups in the bin: ineligible, M=0, null bin.
Bin quality Q=0.69 < 0.70: ineligible even with 3 groups.
Bin quality exactly Q=0.70 is eligible: M = 0.5*1 = 0.5.
cases.derivation: reliabilities 0.5/0.25/0.25 give exact local weights 0.5/0.25/0.25; Q = 0.70*(1.0) = 0.70 meets the gate exactly; S = 1; M = 0.5*1 = 0.5 exactly.

cases.description: Bins u=0.8 (S=0.5) and u=0.4 (S=1.0) tie at 0.4: the smaller u wins.
cases.derivation: exact local weights 0.5/0.25/0.25 in both bins; u*S: 0.8*0.5 = 0.4 and 0.4*1.0 = 0.4; the exact tie resolves to the smaller u=0.4.

cases.description: Bins u=0.4 (S=1, value 0.4) and u=0.8 (S=0.6, value 0.48): u=0.8 wins.
Bin u=0.5 has zero local weight (all reliability 0); bin u=0.9 stands alone.
Bin u=0.7 has 5 items but only 2 independence groups: ineligible. Bin u=0.3 with 3 independent items yields M=0.3.
All three cost terms saturate at the min(2,...) cap: cost=2.0, e=1/3.
successful_use=0 gives benefit 0 and e_j=0; E=0 with nonzero total weight.
Mixed ages, tags, groups, depths, and bins; canonical ordering must make any input permutation byte-identical at 12 decimals.
P=0.20 is below 0.30: level 1 and G=0 even with three groups.
P exactly 0.30 starts at level 2.
P exactly 0.50 starts at level 3 (six groups, moderate uncertainty).
P exactly 0.70 starts at level 4 and G is computed (gate is P<0.70); 12 groups with U_P<=0.50 make the node promotable.
P exactly 0.85 with 20 independent groups, reliability 0.9: level 5, promotable, G>0.
20 groups with reliability 0.4: sum(q_P)=8, U_P=1/3>0.30 caps level at 4 despite P=0.90.
9 independence groups (<10) block promotion and cap level at 3 even with P=1.
P=0.69 < 0.70 forces G=0 and blocks promotion even with M=1 and high E.
cases.derivation: p_j = 0 + 0.25 + 0.20 + 0.15 + 0.10*0.9 = 0.69 exactly; exact weights (4x reliability 1, 8x 0.5, total 8) give P = 0.69 exactly; 12 groups, U_P = 1/3 <= 0.50, but P<0.70 gives G=0 and promotable=false.

cases.description: One item per exclusion class plus three valid items: counts 1/1/1/1.
utilization_u=0.25 is outside {0.1,...,1.0}: invalid, other exclusion.
task_coverage=null marks an empty rubric denominator: the item is invalid.
Local normalization inside bin u=0.6 uses post-dedup q values with independence 1/sqrt(2) for the correlated pair: the bin denominator is 2*(1/sqrt(2)) + 1 + 1, not a raw item count.
